overview: The Complete COVID Collections Act aims to step up efforts to recover money lost to fraud and unpaid debts in pandemic relief programs run by the Small Business Administration (SBA), such as the Paycheck Protection Program, COVID disaster loans, and restaurant and live venue grants. It extends the Special Inspector General for Pandemic Recovery, a federal fraud watchdog, through September 30, 2030, and expands its oversight to the SBA programs. It sets a 10-year deadline for bringing fraud charges or lawsuits over several of these relief programs. It requires the SBA to send unpaid COVID loans under $100,000 to the Treasury Department for collection, to brief Congress monthly, and to testify every year, and it requires monthly Justice Department reports on fraud cases and a public website tracking recovered funds. Money recovered from fraud would go only toward paying down the national debt. As of February 10, 2025, it had been approved by the Senate Small Business Committee and placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say large sums of pandemic aid were lost to fraud or unpaid loans, and that taxpayers deserve a stronger, longer-lasting effort to recover it and clearer reporting on how much has been collected.
against: Critics say aggressive collection of small COVID loans could hurt struggling small businesses, and that the frequent new briefings and reports could pull agency resources away from other work.
